results.title: Autonomous Drones Replace Ground Transport for Sakhalin Fish Caviar
results.description: On Sakhalin Island, the logistics of transporting fish caviar from river headwaters to a fish breeding plant have shifted from the ground to the air. A drone called the Brazhnik, designed by engineer Eduard Abramov, was used to transport biological material essential for fish reproduction, bypassing the rugged terrain that typically complicates the movement of fragile cargo. The primary bottleneck in this environment is the topography. The region's hills and ridges act as physical shields, blocking the radio signals required for real-time manual piloting. To maintain the flow of cargo without a direct line of sight, the system was moved from remote control to autonomous navigation. The Brazhnik operates on pre-programmed coordinates, executing the entire circuit-from the plant to the collection point and back-without needing an active radio link to a human operator. This transition removes the physical stresses inherent in the previous transport chain. Traditionally, the caviar moved via a multi-stage process involving ATVs and automobiles over approximately 35 kilometers of unpaved roads. This method took over an hour and exposed the delicate cargo to constant mechanical vibration and jarring, which risked damaging the viability of the eggs. The drone replaces this linear, ground-based slog with a direct flight path, significantly reducing transit time and eliminating road-induced trauma to the shipment.
